scope: development requirements and hazards; not an execution authorization

requirements.requirement: Nia is the sole installed-package and ownership writer
requirements.hazard: independent APT/dpkg/PackageKit or Nia writers can publish conflicting state
requirements.remaining: connect the actual native executor, GUI and automatic updates; prove absence of other writers in a new image

requirements.requirement: Preserve native dependency and effect semantics without falsified compatibility
requirements.hazard: dropping metadata or executing unmodeled scripts violates update and rollback contracts
requirements.remaining: authenticate baseline and selected artifacts; validate protection migration, bootstrap, every adopted phase, generated output and implicit trigger

requirements.requirement: Bounded staging must retain one recoverable root/catalog publication boundary
requirements.hazard: individually committed file-plan chunks expose a partially updated system
requirements.remaining: Bind the caller selection to authenticated resolver/policy results; validate full relationship and cross-architecture coexistence/phase semantics; resolve effective ownership, aliases and native contracts; connect production authority/effects, whole-generation/effect/trust/recovery CAS pin closure and safe GC and privileged metadata; capacity reservation, fsync/space/power-loss fault tests, actual mount/boot activation and recovery, independent trust rollback

requirements.requirement: Check real mitigation values and exact first-party artifacts
requirements.hazard: a configuration flag or successful build is mistaken for effective protection
requirements.remaining: native image integration, hardware and performance qualification

requirements.requirement: Constrain the read-only Nia observer while preserving its documented observations
requirements.hazard: profile presence is mistaken for actual enforcement or required reads are silently lost
requirements.remaining: connect installation, enablement and updates to native configuration effects; this does not confine all Nia workers

requirements.requirement: Expose only the adopted public command family for Nia-owned management; retain independent external tools
requirements.hazard: aliases or wrappers create ambiguous ownership or present unavailable operations as usable
requirements.remaining: native transport, public packaging, real command output, interactive UI and absence of legacy public aliases in new image

requirements.requirement: Manage native interim fixes in the same catalog and transaction authority as normal packages
requirements.hazard: independent fix database, stale base binding or uncoordinated holds permit inconsistent updates
requirements.remaining: Contract semantics and Debian archive chain, independent time/trust floor, current base, emgr execution and shared holds/ownership; normal-update supersession, interruption and recovery acceptance

requirements.requirement: Keep upload urgency, advisory identity, source fix version, vulnerability severity and authenticated authority distinct
requirements.hazard: upload urgency or a textual advisory match is mistaken for signed fix authorization or absence of vulnerabilities
requirements.remaining: authenticated current advisory intake, full metadata coverage and instfix/catalog integration

requirements.requirement: Adopted commands must match the reference behavior and response interface, not merely parse its syntax
requirements.hazard: different status, exit codes, prompts or output fields mislead users and break administrative scripts
requirements.remaining: per-command output and behavior fixtures, TTY/non-TTY, stdout/stderr, quiet/verbose, locale, delimiter-safe native versions, cancellation, partial failure and recovery; real catalog/executor and UI acceptance

requirements.requirement: Authenticate shared repository supply and persist complete metadata version floors before returning targets
requirements.hazard: Untrusted bootstrap, stale metadata, out-of-scope delegation, partial cache publication or mistaken execution authority admits unsafe supply
requirements.remaining: Production keys and provisioning, independent rollback-resistant trust floor/time, service isolation and deadline, contract semantics, interim artifact Debian archive chain, native CAS/publication-plan binding under the live reservation, actual power-loss qualification and managed-engine integration

requirements.requirement: Support all Debian 13 language and locale targets without changing command grammar, signed inputs, outcomes or transaction authority
requirements.hazard: Translated identifiers or locale-sensitive parsing change authorization or recovery; malformed translations and terminal controls obscure outcomes
requirements.remaining: Complete translations for all pinned Debian language targets; TUI/GUI integration and fonts/shaping/RTL/cell-width/accessibility/IME acceptance, translation review and reference response qualification; English fallback never qualifies as a completed translation

requirements.requirement: Build deterministic original-DEB media indexes without granting installed-state or supply authority
requirements.hazard: stale or partial media indexes substitute fabricated package identity, trust or installed state
requirements.remaining: Authenticated admission, native installed service, complete reference-response qualification, reference-aware media retention and real power-loss qualification
